title: Elasticity Heatmap + Hiring Phases (Q4 2026)
description: Working spreadsheet: combines a price-elasticity heatmap with phased hiring ladder and 12-month budget P&L to show tradeoffs between price moves and hiring cadence. Intended for FY27 planning conversations and sales commitment thresholds.
sheet_tabs: Assumptions | Currency: USD | Model horizon: 12 months | Baseline monthly revenue (hosted API): 1,200,000 | Baseline token volume: 600M tokens/mo | Current blended price per 1k tokens: 2.40 | Baseline gross margin: 48% | Average hiring lead time: 8 weeks | Avg fully loaded cost per senior eng: 28,000/mo | Avg fully loaded cost per infra eng: 26,000/mo | Hiring ramp constraint: max 6 hires/month

Elasticity Inputs | Price change band (%) : [-30,-20,-10,0,10,20,30] | Observed elasticity (middle buckets): [-1.8,-1.2,-0.6,0,-0.3,-0.5,-0.9] | Assumed adoption lag: 2 months | Enterprise commit uplift factor: 1.25 | Churn sensitivity to price increase: 0.4 of elasticity

Price Sensitivity Heatmap | Rows: Price bands | Columns: Scenarios (Low, Base, High) | Values: Percentage revenue delta vs baseline after 3 months | Example rows: -30% price -> Revenue +54% (Low) / +32% (Base) / +12% (High) ; -10% -> Revenue +18% / +9% / +3% ; +10% -> Revenue -6% / -3% / -1% ; +30% -> Revenue -22% / -12% / -6%

Hiring Phases (staircase) | Phase A (Q1-Q2): Focus on infra and SRE - hires: 8 infra, 4 SRE; Phase B (Q3): Product and Sales scale - hires: 6 PM/PD, 10 AE/CS; Phase C (Q4): Ops and Support - hires: 6 Ops, 4 Support; Cost phasing table included with start month, ramp fraction, and expected productivity lag

12M Budget P&L (summary rows) | Revenue (by month) | Cost of goods sold (GPU hours, cloud, licensing) | Gross margin | OpEx (people, office, tools) | Headcount cost by role | Net burn | Runway impact by scenario

Scenario Summaries | Scenarios: 1) Defend price (no change) - slim hiring, focus efficiency; 2) Price cut to win growth (-10%) - aggressive hiring to capture demand with expected revenue +9% after 3 months; 3) Price increase (+15%) to protect margin - selective hiring freeze, churn risk concentrated in mid-market; 4) Enterprise price tiers - maintain baseline price for self-serve, +30% for committed enterprise with 1.2x usage uplift

Break-even analysis | Metric: incremental hires supported per price band | Example: At +10% price, can fund 4 senior infra hires (net of COGS) vs baseline; At -10% price, need to defer 7 hires or rely on 18% improvement in batching/quantization to remain neutral

Monte Carlo knobs (notes) | Inputs randomized: elasticity (-0.5 to -2.0), adoption lag (1-4 months), enterprise uplift (1.0-1.5), cost per GPU hour (+/-15%) | Outputs collected: monthly burn, gross margin, probability(runway < 9 months)

Key Risks & Mitigations | Risk: Underestimating negative elasticity on SMB - Mitigation: pilot price bands on cohort, use promo credits | Risk: Hiring delays lengthen productivity lag - Mitigation: temp contractors for 3 months; prioritize infra hires | Risk: Unexpected GPU price inflation - Mitigation: commit to reserved capacity for high-util pools

Decision triggers (suggested) | If realized revenue delta after 2 months < modeled lower bound -> pause non-critical hires | If enterprise commit conversion rate > 18% -> accelerate sales hires by 2/mo | If gross margin declines > 6ppt vs baseline -> enact price tier for new customers
notes: This is a working model: cell-level formulas in original sheet reference live cost model in repo (see linked GitHub).
Primary audience: CFO, Head of Finance, VP Sales, and GTM leadership. Use during 12/08 planning meeting.
Next steps: align elasticity experiments with Growth (A/B price bands) and Solutions Eng (pilot 3 enterprise accounts on committed pricing).
